name: Ministry of Home Affairs Annual Report
publisher: Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India
caveats: Narrative report, not a statistical volume: tables are embedded in chapter text and annexures, no XLSX/CSV companion.
Security-incident series (LWE, J&K, North-East, communal) are MHA/IB-sourced and DO NOT reconcile with NCRB FIR counts; MHA and NCRB communal-incident state tables differ materially.
Counting basis for 'incidents' is never defined in the report; not FIR-based.
Chapter numbering and table numbering shift between editions, so a year-over-year scraper must key on table captions, not positions.
Hindi and English editions are separate PDFs with different pagination.
evidence: Search results return the MHA annual-reports index at /en/documents/annual-reports plus direct PDFs: AREnglish_24032026.pdf (2024-25), AnnualReport_27122024.pdf (2023-24), AnnualReport202122_24112022[1].pdf (2021-22) and AnnualReport_04_05.pdf (2004-05, which reports 640 communal incidents / 129 deaths / 2022 injured for 2004). Domain mha.gov.in is blocked by this session's egress proxy so no PDF was opened.
how_to_obtain: Plain HTTPS GET; no login. From a network that can reach mha.gov.in, mirror the index page and every /sites/default/files/*.pdf link. Filenames are opaque date-stamped slugs, so the index must be crawled rather than guessed.
notes: Backbone/benchmark source. Useful for MHA's own LWE, communal, J&K and North-East incident series, which exist nowhere else in one place. Not a map layer by itself.

name: MHA Left Wing Extremism Division - LWE-affected district classification and violence data
publisher: Left Wing Extremism Division, Ministry of Home Affairs
lag: weeks to months; district reclassification is announced by press note
caveats: AS OF 2026 THE SERIES IS EFFECTIVELY TERMINATED: after a security review completed post-31 March 2026, MHA states no district in the country falls under the LWE-affected category. The layer is therefore historical.
Category membership ('most affected' / 'districts of concern' / SRA-eligible) is an administrative funding decision, not an incidence measure; districts were added and removed for budget reasons.
Incident and death counts are MHA/IB security-reporting, not FIRs; they will not match NCRB.
District boundaries changed repeatedly over the 2005-2026 window (Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Telangana), so a time series needs a district-crosswalk.
Counts are published as district lists and national/state totals; per-district annual incident counts appear mainly in Parliament answers, not on the division page.
evidence: MHA LWE Division page URL returned by search. Corroborating reporting (Deccan Herald, FACTLY, security-risks.com, Tribune) gives MHA figures: LWE incidents 2,213 in 2010 to 33 up to 21 July 2026; deaths 1,005 to 11; SRA district list cut from ~200 districts (2005) to 0 in the 2026 review; Bijapur, Sukma and Narayanpur (all Chhattisgarh) were the last 'most affected' trio. Page not fetched - mha.gov.in blocked by egress proxy.
how_to_obtain: Crawl the division page for scheme documents and press notes; the authoritative per-district incident tables are almost always in MHA answers to Lok Sabha/Rajya Sabha questions (see mha-parliament-mha-pq-portal). File an RTI to the LWE Division for the year-wise, district-wise incident/death table 2005-2026 if the PQ trawl has gaps.
notes: One of only two genuinely district-level MHA series. Historical map layer: 'Red Corridor over time'. The SRA (Security Related Expenditure) scheme district list is the cleanest machine-extractable artefact.

name: Safe City Projects (Nirbhaya Fund, Phase I - 8 cities)
publisher: Women Safety Division, Ministry of Home Affairs
geo_coverage: Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata, Hyderabad, Ahmedabad, Lucknow, Bengaluru
caveats: The published material is scheme/DPR/allocation text, NOT crime data. No outcome or incident dataset has been released.

The component that matters for a map - 'Identification of Crime Hot-spots in the city' and saturation of those hotspots with CCTV - implies each of the 8 cities produced a geocoded hotspot layer. None is public.
Sanction figures conflict across sources: MHA approvals cited as Rs 3,080.16 crore, project cost cited as Rs 2,919.55 crore.
60:40 Centre:State cost share means half the documentation sits with state police, not MHA.
evidence: Search returns the Women Safety Division subpage /en/divisionofmha/women-safety-division/safe-city-projects, the commoncontent page, a 2018 MHA press release PDF (Rs 194.44 crore Lucknow Safe City), and PIB release relid=188078. Eight cities confirmed across MHA, PIB and Drishti IAS summaries.
how_to_obtain: Public docs via HTTPS GET. For the hotspot layers: RTI to each Safe City PMU / the state police Safe City Project Director asking for (a) the list of hotspot locations with coordinates used for camera siting, (b) ICCC camera inventory with lat/long. Expect s.8(1)(g)/(h) security exemptions; appeal on the ground that camera locations are visible in public space.
notes: Best single lever in this domain for sub-city geography. The CCTV/ICCC camera inventories are a ready-made point layer if any state releases them.

name: Nirbhaya Fund - allocations, sanctions and utilisation
publisher: Department of Economic Affairs (MoF), administered with MHA and MWCD
caveats: Money, not crime. Only useful as an exposure/intervention covariate or to date when a city got CCTV/ERSS.
Chronic underutilisation makes 'sanctioned' a poor proxy for 'deployed' - e.g. of Rs 587 crore allocated to Sambal in 2021-22 only ~Rs 183 crore (31%) was used.
Fund is split across MHA, MWCD, MoRTH, Railways and MeitY, so no single consolidated table exists outside Parliament answers.
evidence: MHA 'Nirbhaya/ERSS Section' page URL returned by search. Wikipedia's Nirbhaya Fund article (fetched) confirms the Rs 1,000 crore 2013 corpus, DEA administration, the Rs 194.44 crore Lucknow Safe City sanction and the 31% Sambal utilisation figure for 2021-22.
how_to_obtain: Public pages; the consolidated scheme-wise/state-wise allocation-vs-utilisation tables are reliably tabled as annexures to MHA and MWCD Parliament answers each session.
notes: Context layer only. Its real value is as an index of which MHA PQ annexures to mine.

name: Emergency Response Support System (ERSS) / Dial 112
publisher: Ministry of Home Affairs (Nirbhaya/ERSS Section) and State Emergency Response Centres
geo_coverage: all States/UTs (state-operated ERCs on a common MHA platform)
lag: realtime internally; published aggregates lag 6-24 months
caveats: The underlying records ARE geocoded incident points: ERSS runs GIS-based Computer Aided Dispatch with dynamic map updating, over 10 intake channels (voice, SMS, SOS, email, web, chatbot, media crawler, IoT, WhatsApp, external signals).
NOTHING point-level is published. Public output is national/state annual call totals, mostly via Parliament answers and data.gov.in.
A 112 call is a distress call, not a crime. Huge share is medical, fire, road accident, prank and test calls. Treating call density as crime density would be badly misleading.
Call volume tracks awareness and channel integration (child helpline, cyber helpline mergers) more than underlying incidence - e.g. Haryana April 2025 6,06,039 calls vs April 2024 5.35 lakh.
Each state runs its own instance (e.g. rj.erss.in) with its own schema and retention; there is no single national record store to request.
evidence: 112.gov.in landing/about/features/faq URLs and MHA's ERSS page returned by search; MHA describes a state-centric system with GIS-based CAD. data.gov.in resource 'Year-wise Details of Number of Calls received on Emergency Number 112 from 2020-21 to 2022-23' exists and is explicitly derived from Rajya Sabha Session 262 answers. Haryana ERSS reported 2.31 crore calls attended since inception and 46.6 lakh vehicle dispatches. Neither 112.gov.in nor data.gov.in was fetchable - both blocked by egress proxy.
how_to_obtain: Public aggregates: data.gov.in resource pages and MHA PQ annexures. For anything finer: RTI to the State Police ERSS/ERC nodal officer of a single state asking for monthly counts of 112 calls by call-category and by police-station jurisdiction (NOT caller identity, NOT coordinates) - framing it as jurisdiction-level counts defeats the privacy objection. Start with one cooperative state (Rajasthan, Kerala, Telangana) rather than MHA centrally, since MHA does not hold the records.
notes: Highest theoretical value in this whole domain and the hardest to get. If even one state releases police-station-level monthly 112 call counts by category, that is a police.uk-shaped product on its own. Treat as the flagship Phase-2 RTI.

name: Cyber & Information Security Division / Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre (I4C)
publisher: CIS Division, Ministry of Home Affairs / I4C (attached office of MHA since 1 July 2024)
lag: published only via PIB releases and PQ answers
caveats: I4C's Samanvaya platform is an MIS/data repository with interstate crime-criminal linkage analytics - i.e. a rich internal dataset that is not published in any form.
Headline numbers are released as PIB soundbites, not as tables: e.g. Rs 7,130 crore saved across 23.02 lakh complaints, 16,840 arrests, 1,05,129 investigation-assistance requests.
NCRP complaints are citizen complaints, not FIRs; the complaint-to-FIR conversion ratio is low and varies by state, so complaint counts overstate registered cybercrime.
Cybercrime has no meaningful victim-location-equals-offence-location property; mapping it to the victim's district is analytically weak and should be labelled as such.
evidence: MHA CIS Division I4C scheme page URL and PIB release PRID=2205201 ('Cyber security and financial fraud combat') returned by search; india.gov.in and MyBharat pages corroborate I4C's 1 July 2024 status change and NCRP/1930 helpline architecture. Pages not fetched (egress-blocked).
how_to_obtain: PIB releases and MHA PQ answers for aggregates. For state/district complaint counts, RTI to I4C, or mine the recurring MHA PQ on 'cyber crime complaints registered on NCRP, State/UT-wise' which is answered nearly every session with an annexure table.
notes: Another agent is likely covering NCRB cyber heads. Flagged here because I4C sits in MHA and its PQ annexures are a separate, more current series than NCRB.

name: National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (NCRP) / helpline 1930
publisher: Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre (I4C), MHA
caveats: Portal is a reporting front-end, not a statistics publisher; no public counts page was confirmed.
Complaint counts are not crime counts.
evidence: cybercrime.gov.in described as the NCRP across india.gov.in / MyBharat / MHA pages returned by search; the portal's own domain was not reachable from this session.
how_to_obtain: State/UT complaint tables come out through MHA Parliament answers; RTI to I4C for district breakdowns.
notes: Hand-off candidate if a dedicated cyber agent exists.

name: MHA Parliament Questions and Answers archive (MHA1/Par2017)
publisher: Parliament Section, Ministry of Home Affairs
geo_coverage: all-India; answers frequently carry State/UT and district annexures
lag: answer PDF posted within days of the sitting
caveats: URL scheme is NOT stable across years: 2018 answers sit under .../pdfs/par2018-pdfs/ls-11122018/156.pdf (lowercase house, hyphen) while 2023/2025 use .../par2023-pdfs/RS05042023/3734.pdf and .../par2025-pdfs/LS18032025/2946.pdf (uppercase, no hyphen). Do not guess - crawl the per-sitting HTML index.
Per-sitting index pages exist in English and Hindi variants (e.g. Rs-02082023-hindi.html), so de-duplicate.
Answers are text PDFs for the reply but annexure tables are often image-only or badly laid out; table extraction is the real cost.
The same question is often answered with 'data is not maintained centrally' - a large share of hits are duds.
MHA answers on incidents (communal, LWE, J&K) are IB-sourced and do not reconcile with NCRB.
evidence: Search returned the MHA PQ index 'Parliament questions and answers' at /MHA1/Par2017/PArQueAnsPage-new.html, a per-sitting index at /MHA1/Par2017/Rs-02082023-hindi.html, and three concrete answer PDFs under the deterministic pdfs/par<YYYY>-pdfs/<HOUSE><DDMMYYYY>/<QNO>.pdf tree (RS 3734 of 05-04-2023, LS 2946 of 18-03-2025, LS 156 of 11-12-2018). services.india.gov.in lists 'Answers to Parliament Question-MHA' as a national service. mha.gov.in is egress-blocked so no PDF was opened.
how_to_obtain: Crawl https://www.mha.gov.in/MHA1/Par2017/PArQueAnsPage-new.html -> per-sitting index pages -> per-question PDFs. Politely rate-limit (1 req/2s); this is a small static tree, roughly 8 sessions/2 houses x ~20 sitting days x ~100 answers.
notes: This is the single most under-used source in the brief. MHA hosts its own answer PDFs in a crawlable tree, which sidesteps the sansad.in API entirely and gives you the ministry-filtered subset for free.

name: Digital Sansad Lok Sabha Questions API (api_ls/question)
publisher: Lok Sabha Secretariat / NIC (sansad.in)
time_start: 13th Lok Sabha (1999) for session metadata; full Q&A robust from 16th LS
caveats: Undocumented API reverse-engineered from the Next.js bundle; parameter names are unstable and the endpoint is misspelled ('qet', not 'get'). Treat as breakable.
Some routes are Referer-checked and return an HTML error page instead of JSON without Referer: https://sansad.in/ls/questions/questions-and-answers.
questionText and answerText are frequently null; the authoritative content is the PDF at questionsFilePath.
Statistical annexures are inside those PDFs, often as multi-page tables; extraction needs Camelot/Marker plus a vision-LLM fallback (the livelifelively pipeline does exactly this two-stage split).
Question numbers restart each Lok Sabha term, so (lokNo, sessionNo, quesNo) is the only safe key.
No full-text search over answers exists server-side; keyWord matches subject/metadata only.
evidence: Endpoint, parameters and response schema corroborated across six independent open-source clients whose source I read: GET https://sansad.in/api_ls/question/qetFilteredQuestionsAns with loksabhaNo, sessionNumber, pageNo, pageSize, locale=en, ministryCode, keyWord. Response is a single-element array; data[0].listOfQuestions plus data[0].totalRecordSize. Record schema (livelifelively/pipeline.loksabha-qna, SourceParliamentQuestion): quesNo, subjects, lokNo, member[], ministry, type (STARRED|UNSTARRED), date, questionText, answerText, answerTextHindi, questionsFilePath, questionsFilePathHindi, sessionNo, supplementaryQuestionResDtoList, supplementaryType. Sibling routes: /api_ls/question/qetAllQuestions, /api_ls/business/AllLoksabhaAndSessionDates, /api_ls/member/{mpsno}?locale=en, /api_ls/debate/debate-search, /api_ls/debate/text-of-debate, /api_ls/committee/lsRSAllReports. sansad.in itself is egress-blocked from this session, so the API was not called.
how_to_obtain: GET with headers User-Agent: <project>/1.0 and Referer: https://sansad.in/ls/questions/questions-and-answers. Page with pageNo/pageSize (200-500 works). Filter by ministryCode for MHA, or sweep keyWord over a crime vocabulary. Then fetch each questionsFilePath PDF.
notes: Primary mining channel. Pair with the MHA-hosted mirror (mha-parliament-mha-pq-portal) for redundancy when the API shape changes.

name: Rajya Sabha Questions - rsdoc.nic.in Search_Questions and sansad.in RS Q&A
publisher: Rajya Sabha Secretariat / NIC
caveats: rsdoc.nic.in/Question/Search_Questions takes a raw SQL fragment in a whereclause query parameter (e.g. ses_no>=265 and ses_no<=271, or (qtitle LIKE '%crime%' OR qn_text LIKE '%crime%')). It is a SQL-injection surface by design - query it read-only, never probe it, and expect it to be patched or withdrawn without notice.
Full question text IS returned (qn_text, qtitle) but answer text is null for every record - answers are PDF-only. This is the inverse of the LS API's weakness.
One row per question-member pairing, so a question with multiple askers is duplicated; de-duplicate on (ses_no, question number).

Rajya Sabha answers are also bundled per sitting day as large session-replies PDFs (e.g. the 266th session Winter 2024 replies volume on the S3WAAS CDN), which is often easier to fetch than per-question files.
evidence: Endpoint and whereclause syntax confirmed from two independent open-source clients (CMHLP/archive archive/rajyasabha/scraper.py, which defaults to searching fields qtitle and qn_text; ForPublicOrg/rankyourpolitician, which builds ses_no/mp_code clauses). herrrickshaw/lok-rajya-sabha-qa README (fetched) reports 24,661 RS question records for sessions 265-271 with full question text, ministry, MP code, type and date, and answer text null for every record. Per-sitting RS question-list PDFs confirmed at cms.rajyasabha.nic.in/UploadedFiles/Questions/QuestionsList/<session>/..., and a session-replies volume at cdnbbsr.s3waas.gov.in for the 266th session. All three domains egress-blocked here.
how_to_obtain: GET rsdoc.nic.in/Question/Search_Questions?whereclause=<url-encoded SQL predicate>. Then pull answer PDFs from cms.rajyasabha.nic.in or the S3WAAS session-replies volumes.
notes: Use RS for discovery (full text searchable) and LS for structure. Together they cover the same MHA answers twice.

name: Answers Data of Rajya Sabha Questions (data.gov.in, per session)
publisher: Parliament Section, MHA / NIC Open Government Data Platform
geo_coverage: all-India; individual resources are often State/UT-wise tables
caveats: Coverage is patchy: only the answers whose annexures a ministry chose to upload become OGD resources. It is a convenience layer, not a complete mirror of Q&A.
One catalog per session means ~8 catalogs a year to watch; there is no cross-session search over these tables.
Resource titles are the only description; column headers are inconsistent between ministries and sessions.
OGD API needs a free api-key (data.gov.in registration).
evidence: Search returned catalog pages for Rajya Sabha sessions 234, 239, 250, 254, 256, 258, 259, 263 and 265 under /catalog/answers-data-rajya-sabha-questions-session-<N>, described as questions' answers data provided by ministries/departments under NDSAP and maintained by the Parliament Section of the Ministry of Home Affairs. The ERSS 112 call-volume resource is explicitly derived from Session 262 answers, and NCW and CBI resources follow the same pattern. data.gov.in is egress-blocked from this session.
how_to_obtain: Register for a data.gov.in API key; enumerate /catalog/answers-data-rajya-sabha-questions-session-<N> for N from ~234 upward, then pull each resource via the OGD resource API as CSV/JSON.
notes: This is the only place where Parliament answer ANNEXURE TABLES already exist as CSV rather than as table-images inside PDFs. Ingest this before writing any PDF table extractor.

name: Open-source Parliament Q&A mirrors and extraction pipelines
publisher: Community (indiavotes, NakliTechie, herrrickshaw, livelifelively, CMHLP, OpenSanctions)
caveats: Third-party mirrors: no guarantee of completeness, no SLA, and licences are unstated on most repos. Use for bootstrapping and cross-checking, cite the primary source in the product.
These mirror METADATA and PDFs, not extracted statistics. The annexure tables still have to be parsed.

Record counts differ between mirrors for the same corpus (34,720 vs ~243K vs ~280K LS question records), which reflects different units (per-question vs per-question-member vs per-shard) - reconcile before trusting any count.
evidence: Fetched four repository READMEs. indiavotes/proceedings-data: four corpora (debates-ls, debates-rs, questions-ls, questions-rs) as newest-first JSON shards (reports-<house>-NN.json, texts-NN.json, manifests, audit.json), states 'LS questions alone is ~243K records and climbing', RS backfill walks ~72 sessions, deploys to four Cloudflare Pages projects. NakliTechie/sansadsaar-proceedings-data: ~57,000 LS speech-level debate records and ~280,000 LS per-question records, sourced from sansad.in api_ls/* and api_rs/*, 1,348 commits, served at sansadsaar-proceedings.naklitechie.com. herrrickshaw/lok-rajya-sabha-qa: 34,720 LS question records and 24,661 RS records (sessions 265-271). livelifelively/pipeline.loksabha-qna: two-stage extraction - Marker for text plus Camelot for table detection locally, then Gemini vision only for documents where tables were detected, output as markdown plus question.progress.json.
how_to_obtain: git clone; or fetch the JSON shards over HTTPS from the published Pages domains.
notes: Use livelifelively's two-stage design as the template for our own annexure-table extractor: cheap local table DETECTION first, vision-LLM only on the detected subset.

name: Data on Police Organisations (DoPO)
publisher: Bureau of Police Research & Development (BPR&D), MHA
caveats: Counts are SANCTIONED strength/stations, with actual strength given separately; the two are routinely conflated in secondary reporting.

18,284 sanctioned police stations as on 01.01.2024 (9,127 rural, 5,492 urban, 3,665 special-purpose). Special-purpose stations (railway, women, cyber, SC/ST, traffic) have NO territorial jurisdiction and must be excluded from any geographic denominator.
PDF-only. Tables are laid out for print, with merged headers and footnote asterisks; every edition needs its own parser.
Snapshot is as-on 1 January, but states report at different times and some report late or not at all; missing cells are common and are not flagged.
The publication gives station COUNTS by state, not a station roster with addresses or coordinates. Whether any edition breaks stations down by district could not be verified here.
Definitions of 'police station' vs 'outpost' vs 'police post' differ across states, so cross-state station density is not comparable without care.
evidence: BPR&D DoPO pages exist at /page/dopo and /page/data_on_police_organization_dopo, with companion table pages /page/table_b, /page/table_c, /page/table_d and /page/documents_by_statesuts. BPR&D's own X account (@BPRDIndia, 1 July 2025) states the Home Minister launched DoPO as on 01.01.2024 and DIPTI as on 31.03.2024 at Bharat Mandapam. Secondary reporting gives 18,284 sanctioned police stations with the rural/urban/special split. Annual since 1986, covering manpower, infrastructure, vehicles and police stations. bprd.nic.in is egress-blocked from this session so no PDF was opened.
how_to_obtain: Plain HTTPS GET of the edition PDFs linked from /page/dopo. For a station ROSTER rather than counts, DoPO will not help - see the seed lead on CCTNS/ICJS station directories.
notes: Best available denominator for normalising crime counts by policing capacity, and the only national series for women police, vehicles and station counts. Priority 4 as a denominator, not as a map layer.

name: DIPTI - Directory of Indian Police Training Institutions
publisher: Bureau of Police Research & Development (BPR&D), MHA
caveats: Training institutions, not crime. Addresses are given as postal text, not coordinates.
Irrelevant to crime incidence; included only because it is the one BPR&D publication that ships named facilities with addresses, i.e. a geocodable roster.
evidence: Direct PDF URL for 'DIPTI Directory of Indian Police Training Institutions (As on 31.03.2023)' returned by search at bprd.nic.in/uploads/pdf/1716350798_80f5684dfb1ba3181fd5.pdf; the 31.03.2024 edition was launched alongside DoPO on 1 July 2025 per @BPRDIndia. Not fetched - domain egress-blocked.
how_to_obtain: HTTPS GET.
notes: Low priority. Listed so the catalogue is complete for BPR&D.

name: BPR&D Documents by States/UTs
publisher: Bureau of Police Research & Development (BPR&D), MHA
caveats: Contents unverified - the page title is all that is confirmed.
Likely a mix of state police SOPs, best-practice notes and study reports rather than data.
evidence: Page 'BPR&D : Documents by States/UTs' at /page/documents_by_statesuts returned by search; also /page/completed_circulated_to_states and the site search at /find. Not fetched - egress-blocked.
how_to_obtain: HTTPS GET and enumerate the document list.
notes: Worth one reconnaissance pass in Phase 2 to see whether any state uploaded station-level material here.

name: Modernisation of Police Forces / MHA Police Modernisation Division allocations
publisher: Police Modernisation Division, Ministry of Home Affairs
caveats: Budget allocation and utilisation data, not crime data. Context only.
No division landing page URL was confirmed from this session; only a BPR&D-related PDF hosted under mha.gov.in was seen.
evidence: A BPR&D document hosted at mha.gov.in/sites/default/files/2023-01/bprd_0[1].pdf appeared in search results. The Police Modernisation Division's own landing URL was not observed, so it is deliberately omitted rather than guessed.
how_to_obtain: Allocation and release tables for MPF and CCTNS are tabled as annexures to MHA Parliament answers nearly every session; mine those rather than the division page.
notes: Explicitly low priority per brief. Keep as a covariate: MPF/CCTNS release dates explain when a state's reporting quality changes.

name: CBI View FIR / RC register
publisher: Central Bureau of Investigation
geo_coverage: all-India (CBI jurisdiction: consent states, court-referred, UTs)
caveats: Tiny volume: a few thousand cases a year nationally. Statistically irrelevant for a neighbourhood safety map.
Biased sample by construction - corruption, bank fraud, and cases transferred by courts. Not general crime.
Location is the CBI branch (a city), not the offence location.
Several states have withdrawn general consent for CBI, so coverage is politically, not geographically, determined.
FIR PDFs are scans in many cases.
evidence: cbi.gov.in/view-fir returned by search as CBI's FIR viewer. A complementary OGD resource 'Year-wise Detail of Corruption Case Registered by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) 2017-2021' exists on data.gov.in. Neither fetched - both domains egress-blocked.
how_to_obtain: Scrape the view-fir listing; expect a paginated JS form. Aggregate counts via the data.gov.in resource.
notes: Catalogue for completeness. Do not put on the map as if it were general crime.

name: Year-wise Detail of Corruption Cases Registered by CBI, 2017-2021
publisher: CBI via NIC Open Government Data Platform
caveats: Stale series ending 2021.
National totals only.
evidence: Resource page title and URL returned by search on data.gov.in. Not fetched - egress-blocked.
how_to_obtain: OGD resource API with a free api-key.
notes: Example of the OGD-from-PQ pattern; more valuable as a template than as data.

name: National Investigation Agency case data
publisher: National Investigation Agency, MHA
caveats: No NIA URL was confirmed from this session, so none is recorded. Do not assume nia.gov.in paths.
Very low volume (80 cases registered in 2024 per press reporting) and a terrorism-specific sample. Not general crime.
Case pages, where they exist, name a police station and district of registration, which is district-or-finer - but N is negligible.
NIA is reported to be building a national database of bomb blasts, terror funding, FICN, narcotics, hawala and arms smuggling with NATGRID and IB. That database will not be public.
evidence: Only secondary reporting seen: 210 accused arrested across 80 NIA cases in 2024, and a planned NIA-NATGRID-IB national terror database. The agency's own site was neither reachable nor confirmed by a search result URL.
how_to_obtain: Have a human in India open the NIA website and record the actual case-list URL before any scraping is planned. RTI is unlikely to succeed given s.24 second-schedule exemption for security organisations.
notes: Flagged, not recommended. Include only if a terrorism layer is explicitly wanted.

name: NATGRID (National Intelligence Grid)
publisher: NATGRID, Ministry of Home Affairs
caveats: Closed intelligence-fusion platform linking 21+ databases for 10+ agencies. Nothing is public and nothing will be.
Exempt from RTI under s.24 / Second Schedule.
Catalogued only so a future researcher does not spend a day rediscovering that it is inaccessible.
evidence: Referenced only in secondary reporting about a planned NIA-NATGRID-IB national database of bomb blasts, terror funding, FICN, narcotics, hawala and arms smuggling. No NATGRID URL was observed.
how_to_obtain: Not obtainable. Do not spend effort here.
notes: Dead end. Recorded as a negative result.

name: Bureau of Immigration
publisher: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs
caveats: No BoI URL was confirmed from this session; none is recorded.
Relevant crime content would be look-out circulars, deportations, foreigner-offence counts and human-trafficking interceptions - all of which are port-of-entry events, not neighbourhood crime.
Foreigners-Act offence counts are already in NCRB SLL heads, so BoI adds little.
evidence: No search result surfaced a Bureau of Immigration data page during this session.
how_to_obtain: MHA Parliament answers on deportations, trafficking interceptions and visa-violation cases are the practical route; direct BoI publication could not be evidenced.
notes: Low value for a neighbourhood crime map. Flagged and parked.

name: National Commission for Women - Statistical Overview of Complaints
publisher: National Commission for Women
lag: near-current (the dashboard exposes the current year)
caveats: Complaints to a national commission, NOT crimes and NOT FIRs. Volumes are tiny relative to NCRB (7,698 complaints in all of 2025; 12,648 in 2024) and are driven by awareness and by NCW outreach campaigns.
Heavily skewed by state: Uttar Pradesh 6,492 of 12,648 complaints in 2024, Delhi 1,119, Maharashtra 764. This reflects NCW's reach and UP's population, not relative danger.
NCW's own 'nature' taxonomy (domestic violence, criminal intimidation, assault, right to dignity) does not map cleanly onto IPC/BNS heads.
ncwapps.nic.in is a classic ASP.NET WebForms report page: state is carried in __VIEWSTATE, so scraping needs a session and a POST per year/report-type combination.
Complaint state is the complainant's state, which for online complaints may not be where the incident occurred.
evidence: Search returned the NCW 'Statistical Overview of Complaints' page at ncwapps.nic.in/frmComp_stat_Overview.aspx, offering year (2000-2026), report type (Nature Wise, State Wise, Nature Vs State) and per-state filtering; the NCW Annual Report 2023-24 PDF on cdn.ncw.gov.in; and a data.gov.in resource for 2020-2023 workplace-sexual-harassment complaint counts. All domains egress-blocked here.
how_to_obtain: Scrape ncwapps.nic.in with a __VIEWSTATE-aware client (requests + BeautifulSoup, or Playwright), one POST per (year, report_type). 26 years x 3 report types is ~78 requests - do it once, politely.
notes: Another agent may own NCW; if so hand this entry over. Its only real advantage over NCRB is currency: 2026 data is already on the dashboard.

name: NHRC complaint and custodial-death statistics
publisher: National Human Rights Commission
lag: 18-30 months for annual reports; current-year figures only via Parliament answers
caveats: NHRC counts CASES REGISTERED WITH NHRC, not incidents. A custodial death only appears if it was reported to NHRC (which is mandatory within 24 hours, but compliance varies).
Custodial-death series is small and volatile: 176 (2021-22), 163 (2022-23), 157 (2023-24), 140 (2024-25), 170 in the first 74 days of 2026.
Accountability data is close to a null series - one disciplinary action reported over five years (Tamil Nadu), which says more about reporting than about outcomes.
Annual reports lag badly: the 2022-23 report PDF was uploaded in 2025.
Financial-year vs calendar-year basis differs between the annual report and Parliament answers.
hrcnet.nic.in (the complaint management system) was not confirmed as a public statistics source.
evidence: NHRC Annual Report 2022-23 PDF URL returned by search on nhrc.nic.in/assets/uploads/annual_reports/; custodial-death year series and the 170-in-74-days 2026 figure come from parliamentary data reported by ANI and The Wire; dataful.in dataset 18054 'Cases registered at NHRC on custodial deaths' and an Indiastat NHRC complaints series also surfaced. Domains egress-blocked here.
how_to_obtain: Annual report PDFs by HTTPS GET; the current, state-wise custodial-death tables come from MHA/NHRC Parliament answers, which is the faster route.
notes: Hand off if another agent covers human-rights bodies. Kept here because the live numbers reach the public exclusively through Parliament answers - a direct illustration of the PQ-mining thesis.

name: PIB press releases as a statistics channel
publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
caveats: PIB releases are the ministry's framing of its own numbers. Denominators, date ranges and definitions are routinely omitted.
Most 'statistics' releases are verbatim reproductions of a Parliament answer, so PIB is a derivative of the PQ corpus, not an independent source - but it is faster to search.
Numbering is split across two URL schemes (PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=... and the legacy newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?relid=...); both must be crawled for historical coverage.
reg and lang query parameters change the content; lang=1 is Hindi in some paths and English in others - verify per release.
Year-End Review releases are the single densest annual statistics artefact per ministry.
evidence: Three concrete release URLs observed: PRID=2088945 'Ministry of Home Affairs: Year End Review 2024', PRID=2205201 'Cyber security and financial fraud combat' (source of the Rs 7,130 crore / 23.02 lakh complaints / 16,840 arrests figures), and legacy relid=188078 'Safe City Project'. pib.gov.in is egress-blocked from this session.
how_to_obtain: Crawl by ministry (reg=48 is MHA in the observed URLs) and by date. Use PIB as the discovery index and the underlying Parliament answer as the citation.
notes: Treat as a high-recall, low-precision index over MHA statistics announcements. Good for alerting; never cite PIB alone in the product.

name: Commercial mirrors of Indian government statistics (Dataful, Indiastat)
publisher: Dataful (Factly Media) and Indiastat
caveats: Paid, and terms of use restrict redistribution - which is fatal for a public map. Use for validation during development only, never as a published source.

These vendors do exactly what we are proposing: they harvest Parliament answer annexures and publish them as tidy CSVs. Their catalogue is therefore a free index of which PQ tables are worth extracting.
Derived data - errors in their transcription are invisible without checking the source PDF.
evidence: Dataful dataset 18054 'Cases registered at NHRC on custodial deaths' and an Indiastat series 'Complaints Registered by National Human Rights Commission (NHRC)' both surfaced in search. Domains not fetched.
how_to_obtain: Paid subscription. Alternatively browse their free dataset TITLES to build our own extraction target list.
notes: Strategic use: scrape their catalogue titles (not their data) to prioritise which Parliament annexures to parse ourselves.

name: Answers to Parliament Question - MHA (National Government Services Portal listing)
publisher: NIC / National Government Services Portal
caveats: A signpost page that redirects to MHA's own PQ archive; it holds no data itself.
evidence: Listing 'Answers to Parliament Question-MHA' on services.india.gov.in returned by search, describing access to Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha questions and answers for the Budget, Monsoon and Winter sessions. Not fetched - egress-blocked.

notes: Useful only as a stable entry point if MHA reorganises its own URLs.
